root_cause.text: In `net/sched/sch_qfq.c`, `qfq_change_class()` incorrectly freed `cl->qdisc` and `cl` on an error path even when `cl` was an existing QFQ class, causing a use-after-free if the class had not been newly allocated.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `destroy_class:` from unconditional `qdisc_put(cl->qdisc); kfree(cl);` to doing so only under `if (!existing)`, and the commit message explicitly says the existing class and qdisc “should only be freed if a new class and qdisc were allocated, or we risk various UAF.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In `net/sched/sch_qfq.c`, `qfq_change_class()` incorrectly freed `cl->qdisc` and `cl` on an error path even when `cl` was an existing QFQ class, causing a use-after-free if the class had not been newly allocated.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes `destroy_class:` from unconditional `qdisc_put(cl->qdisc); kfree(cl);` to doing so only under `if (!existing)`, and the commit message explicitly says the existing class and qdisc “should only be freed if a new class and qdisc were allocated, or we risk various UAF.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid freeing an existing class on the `destroy_class` error path by only releasing newly created classes.
intent_record.what: In the error path labeled `destroy_class`, the unconditional calls to `qdisc_put(cl->qdisc);` and `kfree(cl);` were wrapped in `if (!existing) { ... }`, so those cleanup operations now run only when `existing` is false.
intent_record.how: This changes failure cleanup so that newly allocated class objects are released on error, while pre-existing classes are no longer freed or have their qdisc reference dropped in this path. It prevents incorrect teardown of an existing class during a failed class change operation.

grouping_result.intent: Avoid freeing an existing class on the `destroy_class` error path by only releasing newly created classes.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes the error path in qfq_change_class() so an existing QFQ class is not freed, preventing the use-after-free caused by incorrectly releasing cl->qdisc and cl when the class was not newly allocated.

candidates.rationale: This frees the class's qdisc on the destroy_class error path. If cl refers to an existing QFQ class rather than a newly allocated one, releasing its qdisc here can invalidate state still in use and contribute to a use-after-free.
This unconditionally frees the class object on the error path. When cl is an existing class, freeing it here is the direct mistake that matches the root cause and can lead to use-after-free.

vuln_statements.explanation: This unconditionally frees the class object on the destroy_class error path. If cl is an existing QFQ class rather than a newly allocated one, freeing it here causes the use-after-free described in the root cause.
This releases the class's qdisc on the same error path. When cl refers to an existing class, dropping its qdisc reference can invalidate state still in use and contribute to the use-after-free.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body includes the relevant error path in `qfq_change_class()`: `destroy_class:` followed by `qdisc_put(cl->qdisc);` and `kfree(cl);`. The vulnerability root cause was that the old code freed `cl->qdisc` and `cl` on the error path even when `cl` could be an existing class, causing a use-after-free. In this commit version, the unsafe `qdisc_destroy(cl->qdisc)` is already replaced with `qdisc_put(cl->qdisc)`, which is the fix described in the commit message because it only decrements the Qdisc reference count instead of unconditionally freeing it. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present conceptually in the error path, but the code already contains the fix, so this commit is not bug-introducing.
